Services

Services

Tuning is recommended twice a year for most people (more often for more demanding players). If that’s not financially feasible, tuning at least once a year can help keep your piano’s tuning stable longer and helps avoid or address problems early.

Often, when part of a piano is not working right or doesn’t feel or sound right, I recommend having me come tune it as part of a repair or regulation service. Let me know as specifically as you can what’s happening with your piano, and I can assess further at the appointment.

Not sure what you need? Book a standard tuning for now, or Contact me any time.

Standard Tuning

Fine tuning to standard pitch (recommended every 6-12 months). Adjusts for changes due to seasonal humidity and playing. It may include a minor pitch correction if one section of the piano is further out of tune/off pitch.

Standard Tuning with Pitch Correction

A full pitch correction before the fine tuning. If you are unsure whether your piano needs this, choose the Standard Tuning above and I will assess the pitch when I visit. Appropriate and often necessary if:

  • your piano has not been tuned in more than a year
  • if I find the pitch is off substantially from standard (A-440)

Repairs (on site)

Common repairs I can take care of on site: keys slow to return, notes that continue to sound, missing keytops, broken strings, pedal issues, clicks and pops, and more. Small jobs can sometimes be done during a tuning. If your piano has not been tuned in more than 6 months, I recommend scheduling a tuning at the same time.

Regulation (Coming soon)

Adjusts and lubricates many parts to restore high function and smooth playing. Addresses wear, friction, and humidity-related issues. Recommended at least every five years (more often in the first five years or if played more) or if it responds poorly, feels uncomfortable to play, sounds dull or uneven in volume, or makes clicking, popping, or other odd sounds.

Basic Cleaning*

Includes thorough cleaning of keytops, dusting and vacuuming the soundboard and tuning pin area, and wiping down the outer case. (*Completed at time of tuning)

Full Cleaning

Includes elements in a Basic Cleaning plus cleaning the “inside”: the action and action cavity, keyframe, underneath the keys, and the key pins. Regular cleaning of these areas helps keep your piano working well and helps prevent deteriorating function and damage.

Inspection and Written Report

I examine the condition of its parts and function and provide a report with photos afterwards. Report also provides recommended work for improving how it plays and sound quality. This is not an appraisal for insurance or for an expected price of a sale but is often used for selling or purchasing. A tuning is recommended and typically scheduled at the same time.

About

Daniel Ritchie

I’m Daniel Ritchie, a professional piano technician/tuner living in Easthampton and serving Hampshire and Hampden Counties and parts of Franklin Co. and N. Connecticut. I work on grand and upright pianos and give each one the same quality of care. I love making a piano sound more beautiful and feel better to play, it's such satisfying work. Meeting piano owners is fun bonus!

I was trained at North Bennet Street School in Boston, the only full-time, in-person program of its kind in the country. I am also a member of the Piano Technicians Guild.
